prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1235; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, involving two vehicles. Driver 1 was operating the northbound vehicle and stated that Driver 2's southbound vehicle crossed into the lane and made contact at low speed. Driver 1 reported a knee injury, and the mechanism of the impact and the force involved are consistent with that type of injury. Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time of the collision, a fact confirmed by responding officers and by the account given at the scene. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front end of both vehicles that corresponds to the described impact. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of those involved and on the physical evidence. A few older scratches were noted on the lower bumper of Driver 1's vehicle, and these may predate this collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene, and the report will be forwarded for supplemental review.
